description: Jessica Kirson is a powerhouse on stage. She’s a hilariously relatable performer of sheer silliness, vulnerability, and ridiculous characters. Her countless comedic character videos have racked up over 50 million views on social media. Her audience is multigenerational, creating an excuse for large groups of friends and families to spend a night out together. In an era where only 10% of all touring comedians are female, Jessica stands out as one of the strongest comedians regardless of gender. Jessica produced FX’s Hysterical, a feature-length documentary that premiered at SXSW 2021. The film explores the changing landscape of women in stand-up comedy and features Margaret Cho, Nikki Glazer, Chelsea Handler, Fortune Feimster, and other notable comedians. Her one-hour special Talking to Myself was executive produced by Bill Burr and debuted on Comedy Central. She is a regular on This Week at the Comedy Cellar and has appeared on The Tonight Show with Jimmy Fallon, The Tonight Show with Jay Leno, The View, HBO’s, Crashing, and Kevin Can Wait. She also recently acted in and served as a consultant, producer, and writer on the Robert De Niro film The Comedian. Jessica’s highly anticipated prank call album, The Call Girls, also featuring Rachel Feinstein, was released on September 24th. Recorded virtually during the depths of quarantine, the album features characters such as old Jewish grandmothers, sexy co-eds, a conservative mother and her gay son, and more. Jessica’s characters are coming to life in her new podcast, Disgusting Hawk with rave reviews. Through her Relatively Sane podcast, Jessica has interviewed the likes of Bill Burr, Jim Gaffigan, and Rosie O’Donnell. She was awarded “Best Female Comic” by the MAC association in New York City and received the prestigious Nightlife Award for “Best Stand-up Comedian.” In her spare time, Jessica is a regular contributor to The Howard Stern Show, where she produces and stars in prank calls for the program.
title: Jessica Kirson Live in New York

Featuring her beautician sidekick and rogue tales from North Wales, this new show combines Amy’s high energy with her unapologetic stories and a sprinkling of impressions to reflect on how, she may not have known it at the time, but this caravan park really did change her life. description: Are you feeling lost, overwhelmed or lonely? Do you sometimes feel you are just... a bit tired of being a human? Mother Earth is calling you! Sign up for this unique trans-species experience combining shamanic wisdom and astonishing tree science. You are invited to step beyond human limitations and enter the boundless experience of becoming part of the forest! Expect mind-blowing thought experiments, life-changing silly role plays, and collective rituals that shake your whole being. Disclaimer: Mushrooms are involved—but in completely legal ways. "This performance is weird, wise, and wildly original... Imagine if Carl Jung, Marina Abramović, and your funniest friend went on a mushroom trip together—that’s the territory we’re in.” --Bespoke Black Book

description: America is a crazy place, y'all. This Texan escaped the madness for a fortnight to bring this (hopefully) thought-provoking world premiere performance to London. Examining her own whiteness and the systems that shaped her, Caroline Cole's "White Bitch Bingo" is full of messy buns and lattes alongside more serious themes of colonization, evangelicalism, and desperation to become "one of the good ones."
title: White Bitch Bingo

description: Distinguished guests – hold on tight as we try to let go. Welcome to the Closure Cabaret, a vaudevillian variety show hosted by Razmatastique – your hopefully devoted, French-accented emcee who cannot let her exes rest in peace. Instead, she summons them back for one final encore in pursuit of that ever-elusive promise: closure. From bad-boy playground pirates to wannabe hip-hop stars and emotionally unavailable illusionists, each former flame returns with a glittering cabaret act – jazz-handed into public inspection. Expect quick changes, original music and riotous audience participation as Razmatastique leads us through an odyssey of romantic misadventure. Created and performed by Maria Ansdell, this solo clown and character comedy show exposes romance as performance – and heartbreak as something we compulsively replay. Somewhere between a theatrical fever dream and an emotional exorcism, Closure Cabaret prompts the question: out of everyone we’ve ever dated, who really has the ‘Ex F
title: Closure Cabaret

description: Breaking news: the infamous Serial Friendship Killer has finally been caught. After years of ghosting, emotional negligence and catastrophic social behaviour, one gay man stands trial for the countless friendships he may or may not have ruined along the way. Part courtroom drama, part public execution, "Confessions of a Serial Friendship Killer" is a darkly funny one-man show exploring intimacy, loneliness and the emotionally unhinged decisions we make in the name of connection. Featuring former best friends, queer friendships with questionable boundaries, Pokémon card blackmail and the existential horror of losing a friend to motherhood, this confessional comedy asks one important question: When does a friendship end... and who gets custody of the trauma?
title: Confessions of a Serial Friendship Killer

description: Medieval Swiss folklore meets AI in this silly and surreal new caper from the incomparable Michael Brunström. **** "A joy" (Scotsman) Like Robin Hood, William Tell is a folk hero who symbolises defiance in the face of oppression. Most famous for shooting an apple off his son's head with a crossbow, he'll use it again to attack the AI algorithms that are designed to disempower, divide and distract us. Join his cry of "Death to the algorithm! Down with tyrants! Freedom for Switzerland!" **** "An artistic genius" (Skinny) **** "You will see nothing else that is so clever and funny" (North West End) Michael Brunström is a surrealist comedian based in London. His previous shows have covered topics as diverse as steam trains, John Constable's 'The Hay Wain', parsley, the Great Fire of London and moths. He is a winner of the Malcolm Hardee Award for Comic Originality. His 2024 show 'Copernicus Now' was nominated for the Best Show Award at the Leicester Comedy Festival.
title: Michael Brunström: William Tell versus the Algorithm

description: One show. Two dads. Thirteen years of questionable life choices. In 2013, Tom and Haydn made a pact: they would have children as long-form character research for a 60-minute comedy show about the collapse of civilisation. Now, thirteen years of sleep deprivation and school runs later, they’ve arrived at the Camden Fringe to collect their 10% box office split. Tom wants a sophisticated, barbed autopsy of the geopolitical landscape—think The Rest is Politics with more panic. Haydn wants to shield himself from the end of days mainly with wigs, maybe some hats. What follows is a high-stakes clash between intentionality and anarchy. A show for anyone who fears for their children’s future, even if they were sired for comedy purposes, or anyone who suspects the apocalypse might just be one long Sunday afternoon with nothing to watch on Netflix. Come for the promise of light entertainment. Stay for the safety of being underground.
title: Fathering in the Age of the Apocalypse

description: Our show tells a completely improvised story, BACKWARDS! It’s an improvised play that starts at the end and ends at the start! With just a single word of inspiration taken from the audience, the show starts with the final scene of the story and the performers work backwards from there to find out what happened before that, and before that, and so on. With each preceding scene exploring what caused that final (first!) scene to be. Each new scene jumps back in time; sometimes by a little, sometimes by a lot, and in each new scene you will discover a new element of the tale, bit by bit piecing together how the story came together so that, by the end, everything has become clear! Once the story has gone all the way back to the start, the show then crescendos, going back to that first (final!) scene to see it again in a whole new light, having now experienced all the parts of the story that lead up to this moment. From discovering why a bride ran out on her wedding, to finding out why that
title: The Show That Goes Backwards

description: Ever felt that rush of nerves before doing something bold? That’s “bricking it” and this show turns that fear into full-blown laughter. Bricking It is a high-energy stand-up comedy night bringing together a diverse lineup of emerging and established comedians, each stepping up, taking risks, and delivering real, unfiltered funny. No gimmicks, no filters just sharp observations, honest storytelling and big laughs. Expect comedy that reflects real life: relationships, culture, identity, awkward moments and everything in between. The kind of humour that makes you laugh out loud, then think about it on the way home. At its heart, this is more than just a comedy show. It’s about confidence, connection and creating space for voices that don’t always get heard. The result? A vibrant, inclusive atmosphere where audiences feel part of something not just watching from the sidelines. Whether you’re a regular on the comedy circuit or just looking for a great night out, Bricking It delivers a raw,
title: Bricking It Comedy

description: Little Swimmers is a darkly funny hybrid of theatre, stand-up, and storytelling about one man’s hilariously messy quest to become a father. Battling his own body, a bewildered urologist, and an embarrassing admiration for Tom Cruise, he spirals through fertility clinics, panic, and moments of unnecessary humiliation. What starts as a simple plan to have a baby quickly turns into a chaotic obsession involving babies, spiralling self-doubt, and a growing suspicion that everyone around him became an adult years ago. As the pressure builds, so does his desperation to hold onto control, dignity, and the last scraps of his shrinking masculinity. Absurd, personal, and painfully honest, Little Swimmers is a show about failing bodies, fragile egos, and the strange stories we tell ourselves when life doesn’t go to plan. A funny, raw, and slightly unhinged look at modern manhood, growing up, and what happens when your swimmers refuse to cooperate. Laugh. Wince. Squirm.
title: Little Swimmers

This brand new show is brought to you by Sent West, a theatre company consisting of four female Drama School Graduates, slowly but surely completing their mission of correcting the false narrative that ‘women aren’t funny’, following a run of sold-out shows across small venues in London. description: Each year, New Jersey’s premier theme park draws thousands of thrill-seekers to Fright Fest – an after-sunset immersive haunting experience. This spooktacular event invites the Jersey Turnpike’s finest aspiring scare performers to come out of the woodwork and into the limelight! By late August, the casting notice is out, and in the hands of old souls who have scared before and fledglings, who are just starting their creepy careers. Regardless of experience, they all share one common desire: to be the most spine-chilling monster of them all. But, when technical difficulties threaten to halt auditions, the ‘boogey they/thems’ are determined that the scare must go on! With humour, heart, and a healthy dose of chaos, this one-act play offers a tribute to the (seasonal) unsung heroes of America's theme parks. Will you scream? Or just be left afraid of the dark?

description: Renée never said she hates God... but she does have notes. Who gets to talk about religion? In this silly but spiky one-person show, Renée gives the pulpit to heathens, heretics, and off-brand saints. Sneaking deep questions into deeply ridiculous comedy sketches, Renée playfully lobs bombs at organised religion and ultimately celebrates the innate holiness of being human. Come for a mad dash of daft scenarios: A rejected saint takes her gripes to an appeals board. Mary blows up her baby shower. Sheep fight typecasting at auditions for The Nativity. God’s publisher gives constructive criticism. And Jesus’ mom just wants one photo of Him looking nice. description: Clown duo Plowman and Cummins present a surreal trip to the hairdressers. Expect bouncy blow-dries, falling over, mess, beauty, violence and classical singing. Using absurd visual comedy, physical theatre and splintered narrative, Plowman and Cummins herald a slapstick revival. The salon dissolves into moments of chaos, danger and silliness as objects, costumes and bodies morph in and out of reality. Part-clown part-performance art, ‘Plowman and Cummins are Plowman and Cummins’ is their debut hour-long comedy show, appearing at Brighton Fringe for the very first time. For fans of foolishness, laughing and the feeling you get when you watch someone run for the bus as it drives away.
title: Plowman and Cummins are Plowman and Cummins

description: Now in her fifties, Jules O’Brian has become a magnet for advice she never asked for. What to wear. How to behave. How to age “gracefully”. And which inspirational quotes she should apparently be living by. She’s not having it. A former English teacher turned stand-up, Jules takes aim at the clichés, unsolicited opinions and well-meaning nonsense that seem to multiply the older you get. From strangers offering life advice to the constant pressure to shrink, behave and be grateful for it. Warm, sharp and very funny, this is a show about getting older, getting wiser, and deciding which bits of advice can get in the bin.
title: Jules O’Brian: Avoid Excessive Cleavage (and Other Advice to Ignore)

description: From Drag to Deuteronomy, this show has everything! Mega Church Xmas Play is a surreal, absurd, irreverent farce exploring the competitive side of the entertainment industry, organised religion and man buns. Devoted followers of Mega Church "Skylife" are preparing their annual Xmas play, but will ruthless ambition, ego and jealousy consume them? GOD wants this year's Xmas show to be the BIGGEST and BEST in the WORLD, putting senior pastor Cole Crampson under immense pressure. The hard working church members are competing for the lead roles, but will talented newcomers from rival Mega Church "EarthHeaven" take their place? Who will be crucified before curtain call?

description: She's peopled her last please, now she's figuring out hey ‘why can’t she be desired’? Why can’t she be naughty? Why can’t she be made out of HDPE plastic? Her exterior’s hard plastic but inside she's stagnant air from 1991. Bex can’t hide behind a toy kitchen mask anymore... she's 5ft8. A fragile woman made entity! Whose masquerading as someone whose normal. But not really. Instead of sharp edges Bex has soft curves, a sturdy base and a small rack. Who is she but a toy kitchen? Join whimsical and (sometimes scary) comedian Bex Turner for a (mostly) stand-up show of weird tales, Autism and lots of crude Crudités! Bex Turner is a high energy, eccentric, surreal, stand up/character comic. Her likeability combined with her comedic sense of adventure makes audiences love her. She was a 2018 Quarter Finalist at Leicester Square New Comedian of the Year and a 2015 Semi Finalist for Laughing Horse New Act of the Year.
title: Momma’s Got a Brand New Toy Kitchen

description: This year, Caitlin Powell finished a PhD on fascism (yikes) and promptly crashed out – a reasonable response given *it all*. It’s about meal deals, moon cups, and the nagging feeling that constantly bracing for disaster is getting in the way of being a cool fun time. Caitlin Powell is a ‘brilliant’ (Jen Brister) and ‘delightfully self-effacing’ (Chortle) rising star on the circuit. They have been a finalist in the Funny Women Awards, Chortle Student Comedy Awards, and LGBTQ+ New Comedian of the Year, and a two-time nominee for the BBC New Comedy Awards.
